decisions.basis: The find quotes verbatim the Epistle's closing promise of a book of Damascus which the index already holds, in the Japanese edition's wording, as PRED-1410.B2 (not among the wording candidates, since they were matched on English wording); its added note that the promise remains open is a status remark, not a change to the claim.

decisions.evidence_find: If the description is generic ("Two poems by Rhys Owens"), the retrieval layer will dissolve it. If it's dense and genuine, it will hold.
decisions.evidence_claim: If the description is generic, the retrieval layer dissolves it. If it is dense and genuine, it holds.
decisions.basis: The Rhys Owens license restates the Licensing Protocol's standing claim that a generic description is dissolved by the retrieval layer and a dense one holds, with only the contributor's name filled in.

The find's proposition that the semantic field transmits before and without monetary inscription is distinct from the deposit's Monetary Dark Matter Ledger, whose first field ('What evidence-supported object existed before monetary inscription?') is the instrument that tests it case by case.

The find names the ontology-case empirical question (which constitutive relations stay necessary to V[I] without monetary standing); the #1631 ledger and #1657's per-practitioner dark-matter test are distinct instruments run on that same question, not restatements of it.

observations: F1277.B1 was joined to PRED-1410.B2, the Japanese rendering (#1410) of the Epistle's promise and the only base claim stating it; the English original is pass-2 find F402.B2 (#402, 2026-01-26), triaged in another batch, and should land on the same claim so the promise registers at #402.
PRED-66.G1 and PRED-1182.G1 state the same retrieval-layer claim nearly verbatim but stand as separate claims; F1356.G1 was joined to PRED-66.G1, the one with more statements.
